clue.text: Decoration worn by jolly pair in Swiss Cottage

indicators.note: the jolly and the pair are placed inside the Swiss cottage, as the word in says

parts.note: a chalet is a Swiss mountain cottage
a jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
a brace is a pair, especially of game birds

explanation.surface: Someone sports an ornament at a London place called Swiss Cottage while a cheerful couple look on.
explanation.walkthrough: Swiss Cottage is also a district of north London, which helps disguise the Alpine chalet. 'in' puts RM and BRACE inside CHALET, splitting it CHA...LET.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet hung with small charms is jewellery worn on the wrist, an ornament.

clue.text: Sadly this Roman candle lacks one for irregular periods

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the remaining letters are rearranged
lacks means the letter for one is missing from the phrase

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A disappointing firework is missing a piece, causing irregular bursts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks' removes I from THIS ROMAN CANDLE, and 'Sadly' rearranges what is left. A Roman candle is a firework.
explanation.definitionFit: Months of the calendar run from 28 to 31 days, so they are unevenly long spans of time.

clue.text: Advancing years liable to modify …

parts.note: anno domini, AD, is jocular slang for growing old
apt means liable or inclined to

explanation.surface: Old age is apt to change people, a thought that runs on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into 3 down: 'Advancing years liable to modify... 40 to 60 people?'. 'anno domini' as a joke for old age is the convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt something is to change or adjust it to new conditions.

clue.text: … 40 to 60 people?

parts.note: describes those aged between forty and sixty years, read on from the previous clue about advancing years

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 2 down: advancing years are liable to modify people of this age group.
explanation.definitionFit: People in their forties and fifties are in the stage of life between youth and old age.

clue.text: Russian record of excessive bureaucracy

parts.note: red was a term for a Russian communist
a tape is a recording

explanation.surface: A Soviet recording documents the stifling paperwork of officialdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Red tape is the bureaucratic rules and paperwork that slow everything down.

clue.text: Flying cutter

parts.note: a cutting tool that flies, playing on a slang name for a helicopter with whirring blades

explanation.definitionFit: A chopper is both a cleaver and slang for a helicopter, so an airborne version is a helicopter.

clue.text: Fancy fabric father may take to royal home

indicators.note: the father may be added to the answer to give the royal home, so he is removed from it here

parts.note: a palace is a royal residence
pa is a word for father

explanation.surface: Dad might bring some decorative material to the king's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: Read in reverse: add PA to the answer and you get PALACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lace is an ornamental openwork textile, a decorative material.

clue.text: Changes position in the pictures

definitions.meaning: moves something or someone from one place to another
designs printed on paper to be stuck or ironed onto another surface

explanation.surface: Something moves its place within the images.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift something is to relocate it; decals that are pressed onto a surface share the name.

clue.text: Girl arrested you say ? We've got it wrong

indicators.note: you say signals that the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: a miss is a girl, and apprehended means arrested

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a young woman has been wrongly detained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you say' tells us MISS APPREHENDED is heard as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: To misapprehend is to misunderstand, so it means misunderstood.

clue.text: Everybody returns North — useless with no resort

indicators.note: returns tells us to read the word for everybody backwards

parts.note: everybody means all
a dud is something useless
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dejected traveller finds everyone heading north and has no way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns ALL into LLA. LLANDUDNO is a seaside resort in North Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Llandudno is a well-known Welsh holiday town on the coast, a seaside destination.

clue.text: Fur cover one animal provides

parts.note: an animal's coat is its covering of fur
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A creature supplies the pelt for a fur garment.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a long-snouted South American mammal related to the raccoon.

clue.text: Two men of birth

parts.note: Nat is a man's name, short for Nathaniel
Al is a man's name, short for Alan or Albert

explanation.surface: A pair of men are described by where they were born.
explanation.walkthrough: The one phrase 'Two men' supplies both names, NAT and AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal is the adjective relating to birth, as in antenatal or natal day.

clue.text: Fool invests Persian capital? Great snakes, no !

indicators.note: to invest is to surround or besiege, so the fool encloses the other letter

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims 'Great snakes!' on hearing that a fool has put money into a Persian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Persian capital' looks like Tehran, but it is just P. The definition plays on the exclamation: these are snakes, but not great ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Asps are small venomous serpents, so snakes indeed but hardly large ones.

clue.text: "Hollow pampered jades of ——" (2 Hen.IV)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Pistol's ranting speech in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 2: the missing word completes the line

explanation.walkthrough: Pistol, misquoting Marlowe's Tamburlaine, rants about 'hollow pampered jades' of a continent; jades are worn-out horses.
explanation.definitionFit: The line names a continent, the vast landmass east of Europe, home of the pampered horses.

clue.text: Premise DT's as possible source of mental disorders

indicators.note: the letters could be the raw material for the answer, so they are rearranged

parts.note: DTs, delirium tremens, are the shakes of alcoholic withdrawal

explanation.surface: Delirium tremens is suggested as a possible cause of madness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible source of' rearranges PREMISE and DTS. Distemper in an old sense means mental derangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaically, distemper meant a disordered state of mind, a derangement.

clue.text: Mean to affirm life span

parts.note: to aver is to affirm or declare
an age is a lifetime or span of years

explanation.surface: Someone intends to state firmly how long they have lived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb meaning intend, but it is the noun from statistics.
explanation.definitionFit: A mean is the arithmetical midpoint of a set of numbers, the typical value.

clue.text: Nice concert?. No, no! That's odd

indicators.note: the rejection No says the concert is not as written, so its letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as the word no, to be added to the answer to make up the letters

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether a concert was nice replies firmly no, it was strange.
explanation.walkthrough: NICE CONCERT holds the letters of the answer plus NO: rearrange it without one N and one O.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccentric means unconventional or strange in behaviour.

clue.text: Erect sound beams in a higher place

indicators.note: sound here means as heard, so the word for beams is taken by its pronunciation

parts.note: rays are beams of light
up means in a higher position

explanation.surface: Someone puts up sturdy timber beams high in a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective describing solid beams, but it signals that RAYS is heard as RAISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect something is to lift it into an upright position, to set it upright.

clue.text: They scoff like certain birds

definitions.meaning: people who scoff or jeer at others
mocker is a name for the mockingbird and similar mimic birds

explanation.surface: Jeering people are compared to birds that imitate others.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who ridicule others are derisive jeerers, and the mimicking songbirds share the name.

clue.text: Forfeits heads

definitions.meaning: fines or penalties, as at Oxford college dinners for breaches of etiquette
old slang for skulls or noggins

explanation.surface: Penalties are imposed on the leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford a sconce was a penalty, often a tankard of ale, imposed at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Sconce is old slang for the skull and an Oxford term for a penalty at table.

clue.text: Performer makes a poor sitter

indicators.note: poor suggests a bad or broken version, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An entertainer is too restless to sit for a portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges SITTER into RTISTE, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer such as a singer or dancer, a stage professional.

clue.text: Ernie, for instance, a close friend to many

parts.note: a crony is a close friend or companion
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, standing for many

explanation.surface: A man called Ernie is everyone's pal.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNIE was the computer that draws Britain's Premium Bonds prizes, its name formed from Electronic Random Number Indicator Equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie is a word formed from the initials of a longer name, which is the device in question.

clue.text: One lost a ring twice in a river

indicators.note: twice means the shortened word is written two times over
lost means the ring-shaped letter goes missing from the word

parts.note: taken as the word one
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: Someone dropped a ring into a river on two occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes O from ONE, leaving NE, and 'twice' doubles it. The Nene is an English river flowing through Northampton and Peterborough.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nene is a waterway of the English East Midlands draining into the Wash.

clue.text: Therefore has a right to fly

parts.note: so means therefore

explanation.surface: Someone argues that they are entitled to take flight.
explanation.definitionFit: To soar is to rise high and glide through the air.

clue.text: Tree supplies many a coreless fruit

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, standing for many

indicators.note: coreless means the central letter of the fruit is removed

parts.note: an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: An orchard tree yields lots of fruit with the cores taken out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coreless' takes the middle P out of APPLE, leaving APLE; an apple's core is its middle, which makes the surface sly.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple is a broad-leaved hardwood, source of syrup and of Canada's emblem.

clue.text: Rising note I perform quietly on platforms

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: A is a musical note
to do is to perform
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A singer softly delivers a note while standing on stages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns the whole run AIDOP upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Podia is the plural of podium, a raised stand for a speaker or conductor.

clue.text: Part horse, part god

indicators.note: part says the answer is a portion of the words before it

explanation.surface: A creature that is half horse and half deity, like a centaur.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across 'parT HORse'. Thor is the Norse god of thunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Thor is the hammer-wielding Norse deity of thunder.

clue.text: It's rough to be right in a mess

indicators.note: in places the letter for right inside the word for a mess

parts.note: a hash is a mess or muddle

explanation.surface: It is hard to be correct when everything is in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside HASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh means severe or coarse, unpleasantly rough in texture or manner.

clue.text: Possibly a hundred don't need to be maintained

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Perhaps a hundred items need no upkeep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges DON'T NEED (the apostrophe is ignored) into ONTENDED, after C.
explanation.definitionFit: To contend is to assert or argue a point, so contended means asserted or argued.

clue.text: Noel gets 16 greetings

definitions.note: the plural greetings defines a singular object that carries seasonal greetings

parts.note: Noel is another word for the Christmas season
the answer to 16 down is eccentric, and a card is an eccentric person

explanation.surface: A man named Noel receives sixteen messages of goodwill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noel' looks like a man's name. The cross-reference sends you to 16 down, ECCENTRIC, whose noun sense, a card, is an odd character.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christmas card is the folded seasonal message sent to friends, carrying festive wishes.
